editorial.headline: Mushroom Farming With a Clear Bali Opening
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers integrated mushroom cultivation from growing space and media preparation through harvest and post-harvest handling, open nationally to PMA and not blocked in Bali.
editorial.body:
For KBLI 01136, the activity is mushroom agriculture in the practical, production-floor sense of the term. It covers cultivation of mushrooms such as merang, oyster, shittake, ear mushrooms, truffles, and similar varieties. The centre of gravity is not trading, processing, or restaurant supply; it is the farming chain itself, where the operator prepares the environment, manages the crop, and completes the harvest cycle as one connected agricultural activity.

The scope is broad enough to capture the normal working sequence of a mushroom farm. It includes making the **kubung**, preparing or processing the growing medium, planting, maintaining the crop, harvesting, and carrying out post-harvest activities when those steps form one integrated chain. The record also includes nursery and seedling activities for mushroom plants. That matters because this is not just a label for a finished product; it is a registration home for operators whose business model sits inside the cultivation system, from setup and maintenance through the first handling after harvest.

On scale, the record is unusually clean: **Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar** are all open. A founder reading this should treat the classification as available across the full range of business scales stated in the record, rather than only for a narrow smallholder or industrial profile. Nationally, the PMA position is also clear. The activity is marked **TERBUKA**, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of **100%** under the cited presidential regulations. There is no foreign stake cap below full ownership in the supplied record, so the national reading is straightforward: a foreign-owned setup can use this classification nationally, subject only to the facts actually stated here.

The Bali layer is where many KBLI readings become fragile, but this record does not produce a block. Bali’s moratorium rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA island-wide and permanently. Here, however, the Bali status is recorded as **OK_or_HIGHER_RISK**, and the reason given is that OSS risk at **Besar** scale is **Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi**, so it is not blocked by the moratorium. The honest conclusion is therefore positive but precise: this mushroom-farming activity is foreign-open nationally and, on the supplied Bali record, not moratorium-blocked for PMA registration in Bali today. That does not create extra permits, timelines, taxes, or capital requirements; it simply says the classification itself is not shut out by the Bali PMA moratorium recorded here.
